paragraphs: Rav Yaakov bar Avuh said to Abaye: 'When I come from the study house, Father raises a cup for me and Mother mixes it for me; what should I do?' He said to him, 'Accept it from your mother, but do not accept it from your father, since he is a Torah scholar and would feel hurt,' Kiddushin, chapter 1 (31b). In Midrash Ruth, at 'And he shall be to you a restorer of life': R. Yaakov bar Avuh. In the Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 11 as printed (the corresponding passage is 1:9:8): R. Yaakov bar Avuh, in R. Aḥa's name. That matter appears there in Berakhot, chapter 2, mishnah 3: R. Yaakov bar Abaye, in R. Aḥa's name. So too in Tanḥuma, Aḥarei, and chapter 2 of Shevuot, halakhah 6. Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Megalleḥin, halakhah 1, in Rav Sheshet's name. R. Yaakov bar Abaye of Bardalya, chapter 2 of Shevi'it. Bar Abaye, Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah, chapter 1, halakhah 6. It appears that all are one person, and that it should read 'son of R. Abba.'
